Formulation
- Brief summary: Patient presents with an acute three-day history of severe headache with light sensitivity and occasional visual phenomena, consistent with a migraine-type presentation; headaches are impairing daily functioning and work; no psychiatric symptoms documented; plan includes neurological/ophthalmologic evaluation, BP assessment, and consideration of contraceptive-pill modification if migraine with visual symptoms persists; urgent care guidance provided if red flags develop.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Alleviate headache pain and restore ability to work
  - Obtain thorough neurological examination
  - Review safety/appropriateness of current contraceptive pill in light of migraine features
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Confirm likely diagnosis (migraine vs alternative headache) via examination
  - Complete neurological exam and ophthalmologic review; check blood pressure
  - Decide on medication plan and potential contraceptive change if indicated
  - Arrange follow-up and referral if symptoms persist or worsen
- Actions (Patient):
  - Take medications with food as prescribed
  - Book appointment with support line for full examination
  - Monitor symptoms and seek urgent care if worsening
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Prescribe established analgesic alternative stronger than ibuprofen; allow concomitant paracetamol
  - Schedule neurological examination and ophthalmologic/eye review
  - Recheck blood pressure; discuss pill suitability and potential change if migraine features persist
  - Facilitate referral to specialist if indicated

  - Use of medication with food; consideration of stronger analgesic plus paracetamol
  - Importance of blood pressure check and potential contraceptive-pill changes
  - When to go to Emergency Department (A&E) if red flags develop or symptoms worsen
